- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤ 0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly to capture upside potential.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward by 1–3 points.
- If 3+ consecutive days of high sentiment (≥ 0.67) precede forecast, model often fails to reflect mean reversion; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5 points to avoid overconfidence.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price in early 10–15 days; apply upward bias of 0.5–1.5 points for first 10 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend if sentiment is trending.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >2.5 points for 2+ consecutive days, model is likely overconfident; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 point per day until convergence.
